Show paired values

Use scatter for one point per paired observation. If many points overlap, smaller markers or partial transparency help reveal dense areas. An association in a scatter plot does not establish causation.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter([55, 85, 120], [115, 190, 270], alpha=0.75)
ax.set(xlabel="Floor area (m²)", ylabel="Price (thousands)")
plt.show()

Show a distribution with bins

A histogram counts observations within numerical intervals by default. Bin width changes the visible shape. Use the same bin edges when comparing two distributions.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
counts, _, _ = ax.hist([1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 12], bins=[0, 5, 10, 15])
print(counts.astype(int).tolist())
plt.show()
Example output
[3, 2, 1]

Compare centers and spreads

A box plot shows the median and the first and third quartiles. By default, whiskers reach the most extreme data points within 1.5 times the interquartile range from the quartiles. Points outside are plotted as fliers.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.boxplot([[2, 4, 6], [4, 8, 10]], tick_labels=["Store A", "Store B"])
ax.set(ylabel="Units sold")
plt.show()
